role.altitude: The language lecturer keeps practising with students, advising them, choosing texts and deciding curriculum changes; arranging appointments by mail, compiling course results, judging text levels by hand and chasing the bookshop and library shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping reading lists in the library tool
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer who spends office hours on conversation and feedback, not on arranging them.

tasks.short: Let students book office-hours slots, confirm appointments, advise and assist students with language practice and coursework in office hours, and follow up with resources.

steps.what: Student books an office-hours slot on the booking page
Lecturer confirms office-hours appointments with students
Lecturer advises and assists students in office hours: speaking practice, writing feedback and coursework questions
Lecturer follows up by mail with exercises or reading suggestions

tasks.design: Students pick a slot on a booking page linked to the lecturer's calendar, which sends the confirmation, instead of agreeing times by mail. Speaking practice, writing feedback and follow-up stay personal.
tasks.still_hard: Students who only come before exams.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing which sound a student keeps getting wrong.

reach.learn: Whether more students use office hours.

evidence.claim: Booking pages linked to calendars replace arranging times by mail.

assumptions: Boundary: office hours; advising on curricula and careers (task 6344) is a sibling task.
Students' booking time is shown in s1 and is about what a mail took.
Assisting and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of students who book online.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few online bookings; high: most appointments booked online.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather course results and evaluations, evaluate and plan revisions to curricula and methods of instruction, check that texts and tasks match the target language level, revise course materials, and submit changes.

steps.what: Lecturer gathers course evaluations, pass rates and skill scores per assessment
Lecturer evaluates the course and plans revisions to curricula, content and methods of instruction
Lecturer checks that reading texts and tasks match the target language level
Lecturer revises course content and materials
Lecturer submits the curriculum changes to the programme committee

tasks.design: A course dashboard shows evaluation scores and results per skill (reading, writing, listening, speaking) and per assessment, instead of figures compiled by hand. Evaluating and planning stay with the lecturer. A text-level tool estimates each reading text's difficulty and vocabulary coverage against the target level, and the lecturer confirms or swaps texts. The change form for the committee is pre-filled from the course catalogue. Revising materials belongs to the course materials task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were compiled by hand and text levels judged by reading alone.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards and text-level estimation tools.
tasks.still_hard: Literary texts whose difficulty is not in the vocabulary.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a text students will want to read.

ambition.what: Adjust the course after each run.

evidence.claim: An assessment platform provides item statistics per question.
Text-level tools estimate reading difficulty and vocabulary coverage.

assumptions: Boundary: curriculum planning and evaluation; preparing course materials (task 6335) is a sibling task.
s4 is part of preparing course materials, which sibling task 6335 covers; its saving is counted there.
Evaluating and planning keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether evaluations sit in the learning platform.
research_questions: Do revisions follow results more closely?

incremental.description: Lecturer checks the text-level tool against own judgement on sample texts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: results outside the platform; high: dashboard and many texts to check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review new textbooks and materials, choose them, select and obtain materials and supplies such as textbooks through the reading list, and check availability and licences.

steps.what: Lecturer reviews new textbooks and materials
Lecturer selects the textbooks and materials for the course
Lecturer obtains the materials: submits the reading list to the library and bookshop
Lecturer checks availability and licences for digital materials

tasks.design: Publishers' inspection copies are reviewed digitally, which saves a little handling. Choosing materials stays with the lecturer. The reading list is built in the library's reading list tool, which passes titles to the library and bookshop and shows availability and licence status for each digital item, instead of mails back and forth.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lists were mailed and availability chased by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Library reading list tools linked to catalogues and bookshops.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a novel that matches both level and interest.

reach.learn: Whether titles are available at course start.

evidence.claim: Library reading list tools link titles to catalogues and show availability.

assumptions: Boundary: selecting and obtaining materials; compiling reading bibliographies (task 6349) is a sibling task.
Reviewing and choosing keep most of their time.
unknowns: Share of foreign titles the library tool covers.
research_questions: Are titles available at course start more often?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps reading lists in the tool current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many imported titles; high: most titles in the library tool.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review the student's progress and options, advise students on academic and vocational curricula and on career issues, refer them onward, and note the advice.

steps.what: Lecturer reviews the student's progress and programme options before the meeting
Lecturer advises the student on academic and vocational curricula and career issues
Lecturer refers the student to career services or study abroad programmes
Lecturer notes the advice in the student record

tasks.design: The student system shows credits earned against the programme's requirements and open electives on one page, so the lecturer prepares quickly instead of comparing transcripts with the programme guide. Advising and referring stay personal. Keeping the advice note belongs to the student records task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Transcripts were compared with the programme guide by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Degree progress views in student systems.
tasks.still_hard: Students combining programmes or studying abroad.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student see a career that uses their language.

reach.learn: Whether referred students arrive better prepared.

evidence.claim: AI that steers students' education or evaluates learning is high-risk, so no software recommends a path here.

assumptions: Boundary: advising on curricula and careers; office hours (task 6341) and student records (task 6337) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of maintaining required student records, which sibling task 6337 covers; its saving is counted there.
Advising and referring keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the student system has a degree progress view.

incremental.description: Lecturer reports wrong programme rules in the progress view.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: simple programmes; high: many electives and combined programmes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
